h1: Home Staging in Corona del Mar, CA
intro: Corona del Mar is a village inside Newport Beach with its own rhythm: coffee on the highway, a walk down to Little Corona, and a housing stock rebuilding itself one narrow lot at a time. Aviara Design Co. travels from Temecula to stage the new contemporaries of the Flower Streets, the bluff estates of Cameo Shores and Shore Cliffs, and the view homes of Spyglass Hill and Harbor View Hills, each with a different buyer and a different bar to clear.
marketContext: Corona del Mar trades on price per square foot, among the steepest on the Orange County coast. The Flower Streets in the Village are lined with narrow lots that once held a front house and a back unit, many now rebuilt as tall, light-filled contemporaries with rooftop decks aimed at the ocean. Cameo Shores and Shore Cliffs hold the bluff and oceanfront estates, Cameo Highlands and Corona Highlands sit just behind them, and Irvine Terrace, Harbor View Hills, and Spyglass Hill climb the slopes with harbor and Catalina views.

Buyers here already know the coast: Newport Beach families trading the harbor for the village, empty nesters leaving larger Irvine and Newport Coast homes for something walkable, and second-home buyers who want the beach a stroll away. They tour Newport Beach and Newport Coast too, and they have seen enough new construction to spot a staged home that was not thought through.

Two kinds of homes dominate. The first is the new Flower Streets contemporary, tall, narrow, and full of glass, which sells on light, scale, and finish. The second is the older single-level home in Harbor View Hills or Irvine Terrace, often dated inside, which sells on its lot, its view, and the potential a buyer can see. Both need staging, and very different staging.
whyStaging: A new Flower Streets build is white walls and wide-plank floors until furniture gives its rooms a purpose. Staging shows buyers how a narrow footprint lives and how the rooftop deck becomes an evening room.
Bluff and oceanfront homes in Cameo Shores and Shore Cliffs compete with the horizon for attention. The best staging concedes that contest and arranges every room to face it.
Older view homes often carry decades of furnishings that hide the bones. Editing and re-staging lets buyers see the volume, the light, and the view rather than the previous owner's era.
localProof: We travel from our Temecula studio for Corona del Mar projects, bringing the coastal-luxury approach we apply across Southern California. Our portfolio shows our standard for view homes and new builds.

serviceNotes.name: Vacant Home Staging
serviceNotes.note: The service most Corona del Mar listings call for, since new Flower Streets builds and estate settlements come to market empty. We size furniture to the room, keep palettes calm against the plaster and pale oak, and style rooftop decks and courtyards so a narrow lot photographs as a complete home.

serviceNotes.name: Occupied Home Staging
serviceNotes.note: Common in Harbor View Hills, Irvine Terrace, and Jasmine Creek, where long-tenured owners are still home when they list. We edit with a firm hand, keep what works, and fill the gaps with our pieces so the home reads at the level Corona del Mar buyers expect.

serviceNotes.name: Interior Design
serviceNotes.note: For Corona del Mar homeowners finishing a new build, updating a mid-century view home, or making a bluff-top house in Cameo Shores feel warm rather than showroom-cold. Livable luxury with natural materials, quiet color, and a plan that respects the view.

serviceNotes.name: Staging Consultations
serviceNotes.note: A prioritized walkthrough for Corona del Mar agents and sellers, in person or over video. We focus on what moves the photographs: which rooms to stage, what to remove, where to add light, and how to position the listing against other Village and hillside homes.

commonMistakes.title: Furnishing a narrow new build with oversized pieces
commonMistakes.body: Flower Streets contemporaries are tall and bright but rarely wide, and a deep sectional can swallow the main level in a single photo. We choose furniture for the true width of the room, leave circulation visible, and let the vertical volume and the glass do the talking. Buyers should leave thinking the house is bigger than it is, not smaller.

commonMistakes.title: Staging the interior and ignoring the rooftop deck
commonMistakes.body: In the Village, the rooftop deck is often the only place the ocean shows itself, and it is what buyers talk about afterward. Leaving it bare while the living room is dressed tells the story backwards. We stage decks and courtyards with seating, planting, and lighting so the listing sells the outdoor life that justifies the price.

commonMistakes.title: Letting a dated hillside home hide its view
commonMistakes.body: Long-held homes in Harbor View Hills, Irvine Terrace, and Cameo Highlands often have heavy drapery, dark wood, and furniture with its back to the glass. Buyers walk in and see a remodel instead of a view. Pulling back the drapery, lightening the palette, and turning the seating toward the water lets the lot and the light carry the listing.

faqs.question: How much does home staging cost in Corona del Mar?
faqs.answer: Every Corona del Mar quote follows a walkthrough, because the scope changes so much between a back unit in the Village, a rebuilt Flower Streets contemporary, and an oceanfront estate in Cameo Shores. The proposal matches the property and your price band.

faqs.question: Do you stage new-construction homes in Corona del Mar?
faqs.answer: Yes. New builds come to market with bare walls, large-format glass, and no sense of scale. We stage them to feel finished and lived in, warm enough to soften the architecture without competing with it.

faqs.question: Can you stage Corona del Mar homes that are still being lived in?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many Corona del Mar sellers stay at home during the listing, especially in the hillside neighborhoods. We edit what you have, add our own pieces where needed, and prepare the home for photography without a move-out.

faqs.question: Do you really travel to Corona del Mar from Temecula?
faqs.answer: We do. Corona del Mar is a scheduled trip from Temecula, with the drive built into our Orange County calendar. Walkthroughs happen in person or over video, installs are planned around the Village's tight streets and alleys, and we serve Newport Beach, Newport Coast, and Laguna Beach on the same trips.

faqs.question: How quickly can you stage a Corona del Mar listing?
faqs.answer: A Corona del Mar project can usually move from first call to install within a couple of weeks. New builds can sometimes go faster once the home has its final sign-off and clean floors. Tell us your photography date and we will plan backward from it.
